athlete.name: Hannah Coor
athlete.bio: A tenacious outfielder with a keen eye for the game, she blends agility and strategy, thriving under pressure. Off the field, her infectious enthusiasm and team spirit inspire those around her.

caption:
Five years is a long time to give yourself to something. Long enough to change. Long enough to be humbled. Long enough to realize that what you thought this journey woud be... isn’t what it ended up being.

I can’t believe this is my fifth and final year of college softball. I don’t think the weight of that hits until I really sit with it. There were so many moments along the way where I questioned myself, where I wondered if I was enough, or if I was even where I was supposed to be. I learned that growth doesn’t always look like progress. Sometimes it looks like waiting. Sometimes it looks like staying when everything inside of you is telling you to walk away.

There were times I felt invisible. Times I felt like I was falling in ways no one else noticed. I tried carrying disappointment and anger quietly because I didn’t want it to harden me. But the truth is, it did harden me. I became guarded, angry, and closed myself off because it felt safer. I built walls where there used to be trust, and learned how to survive.

BUT GOD!!!!

He met me in the middle of frustration, pride, and hurt that I didn’t want to admit. He was patient. He slowly softened the parts of my heart I thought I needed to protect. He reminded me that hardness might feel like control, but softness is where healing lives.

This journey taught me that faith isn’t about always getting it right. It’s about BEING WILLING to let God undo what life hardened. To unlearn and learn over and over again, to trust after being disappointed, and to stay obedient even when you’re tired of waiting.

From the seasons I didn’t understand, the seasons I wrestled with my identity, the seasons where I had to face who I was becoming, and decide if I liked her. God used those moments to bring me back to myself, but most importantly back to Him.

This year I’m different. More aware. More honest. More at peace. Because God did a work in me that cannot be shaken. The joy of the Lord is my strength. 

I’m grateful for all of it, especially the parts that broke me open so God could rebuild me. Thank you, Jesus. For Your patience and for restoring what needed healing. ♥️

#someday #tyj

caption:
Goodbye 2025.

What a year it has been. I don’t see anything the same way I did at the beginning of this year. 2025 challenged me physically, mentally, and spiritually and broke me in more ways than I can count, but the Lord had ways of using the darkness I experienced to expose the areas of my life that I needed to change. 2025 was so hard for me, and this past year ultimately got me to quit. It got me to quit entertaining negative influences, bad habits, and ways of thinking that made me miserable. I was shown the danger of compromise, the importance of perspective, and the necessity of being uncomfortable. Sitting in the uncomfortable and wondering why God was just watching me be miserable was actually just God proving His word to be true. James 1:12 says, “Blessed is the one who perseveres under trial because, having stood the test, that person will receive the crown of life that the Lord has promised to those that love Him.” I now consider myself blessed to have the opportunity to struggle and experience the faithfulness of God that often gets misunderstood. If I call myself a child of God and His will for His only son included crucifixion, then I shouldn’t be surprised when His will for my life also includes uncomfortable obedience. Faith in God doesn’t mean life will be easy, it just means the struggle now has purpose. Thank you God for teaching, shaping, and guiding me through everything this past year. I’m not the same person I was at the start of the year and I am so grateful for the personal growth I’ve experienced. With God all things are possible. 

2026 is the year to be bold, and I’m ready. #revenge2026

caption:
Come cook with me (and Miko)!! 

What you’ll need:
 
Italian Sausage
1/2 medium onion
4 cloves of garlic
1 cup uncooked orzo
2 cups chicken broth
1/4 heavy cream
2 cups of spinach

1. Brown your sausage in a large pan. Cook for 5 minutes. Then add your chopped onion and cook for 5 more minutes. Add in orzo and garlic , cook for 30 seconds.
2. Add in cream and broth. Let it boil and then cook uncovered for 10 minutes on medium/low heat. Stir often to prevent sticking.
3. Take your pot off the heat and add in spinach. Mix until spinach is wilted and enjoy! 
#recipe #onepotmeal 

If you have any recipes you want me to try let me know!! 😊😊

caption: Sometimes you have to discipline your way out of a hole. For me, that means going for a walk. At the beginning of the year when I was able to walk in shoes again, I started going for a walk almost every day. I knew my foot wasn’t going to get stronger unless I used it. I recorded every single walk and this year, I have walked a total of 1,160.48 miles. I’ve spent this time talking to God, and the way He has encouraged me during my hardest moments when I simply chose to show up, even when I didn’t want to, has shown me how important it is to stay true to the commitments you make for yourself. Now it’s become a habit for me and I’ll continue building on this in 2026:)

caption:
On episode 197 I am delighted to welcome back Oklahoma Sooners forward Emma Tolan. 
Emma rejoins the podcast following her first interview on episode 175 following her announcement to join the Sooners on scholarship. She is one of the many Irish girls putting Irish basketball on the world map and one of two Irish players in the SEC this season. If you haven’t listened to that episode go back and learn about her basketball journey which is key context for this episode. 

While in this episode we catch up on her life since June, how she has settled in Norman Oklahoma, the style of basketball, life as a college athlete in the SEC and more. 
Since recording this interview Emma has gone to feature in multiple games averaging 13.8 minutes in her first year of college basketball. She is an outstanding player and role model for all Irish basketball players. 

This is Spotlight Her — where we celebrate the athletes, the journey, and the game.

caption:
If you’re a future D1 volleyball player… read this or share it with someone that needs it 🤗

I thought playing Division 1 would feel like an extension of high school or club volleyball.
It’s not.
At this level, everything changes.

Nobody cares how many awards you had.
What matters is how fast you adjust, how well you recover, and how mentally tough you become.

The freshman year reality hits hard:
You’re competing with grown women that have played longer…
You may be learning a new system…
And sometimes the expectations aren’t always explained — you’re expected to figure it out. I suppose it’s a taste of the real world 🙃

If you’re dreaming of playing D1, here’s the truth I wish someone told me:
Ask questions.
Recover with intention.
And don’t let comparison destroy your confidence.

College volleyball is challenging…but it will turn you into a completely different athlete if you let it. 💯

caption:
I used to pray these “lasts” would hurry up. There was a time I was so tired, so beat down, so ready to be done with the grind and the pain, that I just wanted to fast forward to the end. I thought being finished would feel like relief. I thought I was ready to move on. But now that the “lasts” are really here… I don’t want them to come fast at all. I want time to slow down.

I want to soak in every single part of this year. The good stuff, the hard days, the little moments I’ll never get back. The laughs in the dugout, the feeling of stepping onto the field, the quiet times in the grass where I remind myself, “you still get to do this.”

It almost feels like borrowed time, and I don’t take it lightly. I’m grateful. I’m emotional. I’m fired up. And I’m soaking up every second God has given me here.

One last fall ball.
One last season.
One last chance to love this game with everything I’ve got.

Now, I’m not rushing toward the finish line. I’m holding on a little tighter and enjoying the ride. 

#someday

caption:
One of the most talented kids I’ve ever coached.

Every lesson she was at, I’d laugh because she was so athletic; everything looked easy. After she moved from shortstop to outfield, I would wonder how long she would keep coming because we mostly teach infielders.

But every week she showed up. She set the standard for effort, and she did every single drill better than most.

It turned out that defense was her safe space. Even when things didn’t go her way, when it seemed like the odds were stacked against her, she showed up, got to vent and reset. She knew she had us behind her all the way.

I hope all the girls we train find this kind of support and this sense of safety.

Start your journey with us this December at Groundwork.

caption: Unko Mitch, hearing that you passed away this most recent Sunday had me in a lot of different emotions. When I got news that you were on your last days I broke into tears that Wednesday Night. I called my Mom, Dad, and my Unko Josh for guidance because all my emotions were coming at once. I felt helpless because knowing you were leaving this world meant a lot of my younger cousins and your grandkids wouldn’t be able to experience on how much of a role model you were for me and my brothers and my dad. You were a father figure to me and the boys and we are so blessed for everything you’ve done for us. When you first passed I had a lot of feelings going towards your grandkids and my youngest brother on how they wouldn’t be able to see on what a great man you are but my Mom and Dad and Unko Josh helped me understand and guide me to keep your name in your grandkids hearts by me and my brothers memories with you. I miss goings to Pounders with you, I miss our Food-land trips, I miss you yelling all the time when you play your card games, I miss YOU my unko but I’m so happy to know you’re in no more pain and that you’ve been reunited with Gramma and Papa Afalava. My deepest condolences to My Aunty Marvel, Aunty Manaia, Unko Sole, and Unko Samala. The things you’ve done for this whole Afalava family will never be forgotten my Unko. Everything I do from this day is dedicated to you Unko Mitch❤️ Me and my family miss you so so much Unko and especially me. I love you Unko Mitch RIL🕊️❤️

caption:
Grateful to be a sooner, thankful for everyone

A Sooner historically refers to a person who entered the Oklahoma lands before they were legally allowed during the Oklahoma Land Runs of the late 19th century.
	•	In 1889, the U.S. government opened up portions of land in what is now central Oklahoma for settlement. At noon on April 22, settlers—known as “Boomers”—were supposed to rush in and stake claims.
	•	However, some people slipped in sooner than the official start, hiding out and grabbing the best plots of land before others had a fair chance.
	•	These early trespassers were called “Sooners.”

Originally, the term carried a negative meaning (cheating the rules), but over time it became associated with Oklahoma’s pioneering spirit and was eventually adopted proudly as the state’s nickname and the University of Oklahoma’s identity.

caption: While growing up, my parents had suspected I had hearing loss, this was because I would slur my words, had to have people constantly repeat themselves, and much more. My teachers never suspected anything was wrong because I had all A’s and never seemed to struggle in my studies. I developed ways to cope, through repeating what someone had said to me to make sure I heard them right, learning to read lips, and self teaching in school. It wasn’t until the fall of last year when I realized that there was something wrong with my hearing. I struggled to hear my roommates in the dorm, struggled to hear my coaches during practice. I finally decided to get my hearing checked over Christmas break, and come to find out I had Bilateral Sensorial Hearing Loss in both ears. At first this news devastated me, I couldn’t understand how this was never diagnosed growing up, and I thought people would treat/view me differently once they found out about my hearing loss. Even more, I never saw a softball player wearing hearing aids when growing up, so I thought that I had just handicapped myself from playing the sport I love to play. While it took time for me to come to terms with the news of my hearing loss, and accepting that I would be wearing hearing aids for the rest of my life, I realized that if I was able to the things I’ve done without hearing aids, imagine what more I can do with them and how much easier everything will be with them. Hearing aids were an adjustment at first, but now I can fully hear the world as I am supposed to. At times it can be overwhelming, especially playing in front of big crowds or going to class in big lecture halls and there are still many steps to taking in adjusting to my hearing aids. New challenges were presented to me when getting hearing aids, and having to push through the challenges while pushing through the challenges of my freshman year playing collegiate softball tested me and would create doubt. But, at the end of the day the work I put in is all still there and now I can thrive through being able to hear. There were many doubt and tears, but this is the journey God placed before me and I choose to keep pushing forward.

caption:
Thank you softball, for being so much more than just a game. I struggle to find the words to express how much you mean to me, have changed my life, and have shaped me into the women I am today. You gave me so much more than just wins, loses, or stats. You gave me strength, resilience, and most importantly, friendships that I will cherish for the rest of my life. You taught me how to fail with grace, how to pick myself back up, and push myself further when things got harder. 
The girl who started her college career 5 years ago was excited and hopeful but that was quickly turned into being lost, broken, and unsure of where the sport was taking her. She prayed that God would take control of this journey and the journey He took her on was so much more incredible than she ever expected.
Through every inning, injury, every moment of doubt, and every celebration, God was there. I know none of this would have been possible without Him and I am so incredibly thankful He chose to bless me with the ability and opportunity to play the game I love for so many years. His plan has always been greater than mine and this journey has been living proof of that. So thank you, Lord, for writing this in my story. I may be sad that this chapter of the story has closed, but I have so much excitement for the chapters that are ahead. 
Romans 8:28

caption:
When I first came to OU, I had no idea how much this game and this place would shape me. I was challenged in ways I never expected. The wins, the losses, the early mornings, the practices, the pressure. It all pushed and tested everything in me. And honestly, I’m grateful for every bit of it.

I’m grateful because my relationship with Christ has grown more than I could ever imagine during my time here. I learned to trust God, regardless of the situation or outcome. I learned that God’s timing is exceptional, and honestly, it gave me a lot of peace in my final moments in an OU uniform.

I’m beyond grateful for the friendships I’ve developed here. This program gave me the opportunity to meet some of the most genuine and inspiring people I’ve ever known, and I’ll never take that for granted. So, thank you for everything. 

Maybe this is goodbye to softball. Maybe it’s a see you later. I don’t know yet, but I do know I’m ready for whatever the Lord has next. 

Cyd 🫂

caption:
Just so grateful. 🥺🤍

As I look back and reflect on these past 15 years, my heart is filled with nothing but gratitude and appreciation. This sport has given me countless memories and relationships that I will cherish for the rest of my life. There have been ups and downs, but every experience and setback has shaped me into the person I am today, and I wouldn’t trade that for anything.

This journey has been nothing short of magical, but it wouldn’t be right to end it without acknowledging the village of people who helped make my dreams a reality:

To my club coaches, I truly don’t know how to thank you all for everything you have done for me. There will never be enough words to express my gratitude. You have all impacted my life in more ways than you could possibly imagine. You always believed in me and continuously pushed me to be a better gymnast and person. You have all become my second family, and it’s been an absolute HONOR to have been coached by you.

To my parents and family, I can’t thank you enough for all the sacrifices you made to help me accomplish my goals and aspirations. You have selflessly put me before yourselves and constantly to do it without an ounce of hesitation. I wouldn’t be where I am today without you, and I feel extremely blessed to have such an incredible support system in my life.

To my Ascend family and teammates, I truly don’t know how I got so lucky. Thank you all for your endless support and encouragement. Thank you for providing me with a second home. And most of all, thank you for the best 15 years. I will always be y’all’s biggest fan!

Here’s to bigger and better things!
See you in the NCAA! ❤️

#grateful

caption:
4.13.25. One of the best days of my life.

I was baptized the first time when I was 11, but my relationship with God has become so much more since then. I didn’t really understand what it meant to trust God, and recently I have found myself asking really hard questions only God had answers to. I’ve learned that it is never my place to ask God why, but only my place to ask Him for strength, because it wouldn’t be faith if I had all the answers. I understand that no matter what I go through in life, God sees me and the things He allows me to wrestle with are to help me become the person He needs me to be. God has ways of working in my life that are beyond my understanding, and I trust that He knows what is best for me, regardless of how hard it might be or the plans I make. There is a reason God asks me to let go of tomorrow, and I’ve learned how impossible it is to have hope in certain situations when I try to predict the outcome. Nothing is too big for God, and I have found so much peace in giving Him my insecurities and embracing the opportunities and relationships He’s given me in the present moment. I’ll miss so much if I’m distracted by things I can’t control or what I wish was different. God has blessed me with so many people and I am thankful for the way they have helped me fight battles they don’t know about. I am so grateful to be saved, restored, and whole in the presence of God. James 1:12🤍

As I think back on this weekend, it’s hard to put into words how I’m feeling! I am overwhelmed with gratitude and honored to be the 2025 Nastia Liukin Cup All-Around Champion! This meet has meant more to me than anyone will truly understand. It’s been an absolute privilege to get to compete with some of the best level 10s in the country, and I wouldn’t trade my experiences for the world! This meet has given me beautiful friendships and memories that I will cherish for the rest of my life! 

I want to thank all of my coaches, family, and friends for your endless support and unwavering belief! I couldn’t have done this without you! I also want to thank @nastialiukin, @usagym, and @ozoneleos for organizing and hosting such an incredible event! You all always go above and beyond to make us feel so special, and words will never be able to express my gratitude and appreciation for everything you do! This weekend was a dream come true, and I honestly couldn’t have asked for anything more! ✨🎀

caption:
Dear Elite Gymnastics, 

Thank you for an experience that has been more than I have ever dreamed possible. 6 US Championships, 6 international trips, 2021 Olympic trials, and a 3x National team member. 

Sadly the time has come to say goodbye to this chapter of my gymnastics career. To all the national staff, you will always hold a special place in my heart. Thank you for helping me become a better athlete, but more importantly a better person. The character you have helped me build is something I will carry with me for a lifetime. Thank you to my teammates for being there for me through all my highs and all my lows. For giving me the confidence and courage to go out there and chase my dreams. You have all been my rock through it all and I wouldn’t be where I am today without you. 

Elite gymnastics has been my way of life for the past 8 years. I will cherish these memories for the rest of my life. But I am looking forward to becoming a sooner and start new gymnastics memories ❤️

caption:
2024 MPSF Freshman of the Year
NICO HAMILTON · FRESHMAN · OKLAHOMA
 
University of Oklahoma freshman Nico Hamilton (Grapevine, TX) has competed in seven meets this season and ranks sixth nationally on the floor exercise (14.083). He is the only freshman ranked in the national top-10 on floor. He was named CGA National Rookie of the Week on March 6 and MPSF Freshman of the Week twice (March 5 and March 12). Despite not competing in OU’s first two meets of the season, Hamilton debuted on parallel bars Jan. 28 at No. 5 Illinois, scoring a 13.800 in his first collegiate routine. He then posted a near-perfect 9.5 execution score on his 14.800 floor routine at No. 4 Michigan on March 2, becoming just the second gymnast nationally to reach that score in the event this year. He went on to score a 14.350 floor and 13.850 parallel bars against No. 9 Navy on March 9. He enters the postseason having scored 14 or better in three of his six floor routines. Hamilton is the first Sooner to be named MPSF Men’s Gymnastics Freshman of the Year.

#MPSF #ALLMPSF #MVP #mensgymnastics

caption:
XZAYVIER BROWN FOR THE AIR JORDAN 11 RETRO “GRATITUDE” 

St. Joseph’s University freshman point guard Xzayvier Brown has a lot to be grateful for, and recently we caught up with him and his sisters as he surprised them with a pair of special kicks. Last February, Brown led Roman Catholic High School to the Philadelphia Catholic League Championship, scoring a game high 20 points - including a buzzer-beating three to send the game to overtime. This fall he moved from Roman’s Center City locale up to the leafy northwest Philly campus of St. Joe’s to begin his Division 1 basketball career, playing in front of his family and friends in the city he loves. It’s for these reasons we asked Xzayvier and his sisters, Parker and Nyler, to help us introduce the Air Jordan 11 Retro “Gratitude” with a special photo shoot in the St. Joe’s locker room.

“I’ve played basketball all over the country, but there is no place like Philly.” 

Xzayvier “X” wanted to give back to the city and the people who had given so much to him. “It’s cool having my family and friends, all the old coaches, people who watched me grow up being able to see me play,” he said. “I’m just grateful to get to be home close to my family and watch my sisters grow up.” 

The Air Jordan 11 Retro “Gratitude” drops this Saturday 12/9 at Lapstone & Hammer.  Hit the link in bio to read more on Xzayvier’s story!
